title: MATH GAOKAO - 340
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Lower Quartile of a Data Set
questions.learningObjective: Compute the lower quartile of an ordered data set using the median-of-halves method.
questions.question: Find the lower quartile \(Q_1\) of the data set \(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8\) using the median-of-halves method.
questions.explanation: Since \(n=8\), the lower half of the ordered data is \(1,2,3,4\). The median of this lower half is \(\frac{2+3}{2}=2.5\). Therefore, \(Q_1=2.5\).
questions.hint: Split the ordered data into lower and upper halves, then find the median of the lower half.

questions.concept: Upper Quartile of a Data Set
questions.learningObjective: Compute the upper quartile of an ordered data set using the median-of-halves method.
questions.question: Find the upper quartile \(Q_3\) of the data set \(2,4,5,7,9,10\) using the median-of-halves method.
questions.explanation: Since \(n=6\), the upper half of the ordered data is \(7,9,10\). The median of this upper half is \(9\). Therefore, \(Q_3=9\).
questions.hint: Split the ordered data into lower and upper halves, then find the median of the upper half.

questions.learningObjective: Compute the interquartile range from the lower and upper quartiles.
questions.question: Find the interquartile range of the data set \(3,5,7,8,10,12,15\) using the median-of-halves method.
questions.explanation: The median is \(8\). The lower half is \(3,5,7\), so \(Q_1=5\). The upper half is \(10,12,15\), so \(Q_3=12\). Therefore, the interquartile range is \(Q_3-Q_1=12-5=7\).
questions.hint: First find \(Q_1\) and \(Q_3\), then subtract the lower quartile from the upper quartile.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the upper quartile when the lower quartile and interquartile range are given.
questions.question: If \(Q_1=12\) and the interquartile range is \(8\), find \(Q_3\).
questions.explanation: The interquartile range is defined by \(\mathrm{IQR}=Q_3-Q_1\). Thus \(8=Q_3-12\), so \(Q_3=12+8=20\).
questions.hint: Use the relationship \(\mathrm{IQR}=Q_3-Q_1\) and solve for the unknown quartile.

questions.learningObjective: Identify the lower and upper quartiles of an ordered data set.
questions.question: For the data set \(5,7,8,10,12,14,15,18\), which pair gives \(Q_1\) and \(Q_3\) using the median-of-halves method?
questions.explanation: The lower half is \(5,7,8,10\), whose median is \(\frac{7+8}{2}=7.5\). The upper half is \(12,14,15,18\), whose median is \(\frac{14+15}{2}=14.5\). Hence \(Q_1=7.5\) and \(Q_3=14.5\).
questions.hint: Separate the ordered data into two equal halves and find the median of each half.

questions.learningObjective: Compute all three quartiles of an ordered data set.
questions.question: Find the quartiles \(Q_1,Q_2,Q_3\) of the data set \(1,2,4,5,7,9,10\) using the median-of-halves method.
questions.explanation: The median \(Q_2\) is the middle value \(5\). The lower half is \(1,2,4\), so \(Q_1=2\). The upper half is \(7,9,10\), so \(Q_3=9\). Therefore, \(Q_1=2,\ Q_2=5,\ Q_3=9\).
questions.hint: Find the median first, then find the median of the lower half and the median of the upper half.

questions.concept: Upper Quartile of a Data Set
questions.learningObjective: Compute the upper quartile of an ordered data set with an odd number of values.
questions.question: Find \(Q_3\) for the data set \(2,4,4,5,7,9,11,13,15\) using the median-of-halves method.
questions.explanation: Since \(n=9\), the median is the fifth value, \(7\). The upper half is \(9,11,13,15\), whose median is \(\frac{11+13}{2}=12\). Therefore, \(Q_3=12\).
questions.hint: Exclude the median when forming the upper half for an odd-sized data set, then find the median of that upper half.

questions.learningObjective: Use quartiles and the interquartile range to identify an outlier.
questions.question: A data set has \(Q_1=10\) and \(Q_3=22\). Using the \(1.5\times \mathrm{IQR}\) rule, which value is an outlier?
questions.explanation: The interquartile range is \(\mathrm{IQR}=22-10=12\). The upper fence is \(Q_3+1.5\mathrm{IQR}=22+1.5(12)=22+18=40\). Since \(45>40\), the value \(45\) is an outlier, while \(38<40\) is not.
questions.hint: Compute the interquartile range, then find the upper boundary \(Q_3+1.5\mathrm{IQR}\).

questions.concept: Effect of Linear Transformation on Quartiles
questions.learningObjective: Determine how a linear transformation affects the interquartile range.
questions.question: A data set has \(Q_1=4\) and \(Q_3=9\). If every value is multiplied by \(3\) and then \(2\) is added, what is the new interquartile range?
questions.explanation: The original interquartile range is \(Q_3-Q_1=9-4=5\). For the transformation \(y=3x+2\), the quartiles become \(Q_1'=3(4)+2=14\) and \(Q_3'=3(9)+2=29\). Thus the new interquartile range is \(29-14=15\), which is \(3\) times the original interquartile range.
questions.hint: Adding a constant shifts quartiles but does not change the interquartile range; multiplying by a constant scales the interquartile range by the same factor.

questions.concept: Interquartile Range with an Unknown Data Value
questions.learningObjective: Determine an unknown data value from the median and then compute the interquartile range.
questions.question: The ordered data set \(2,3,5,7,x,12,14,16,18\) has median \(9\). Find its interquartile range using the median-of-halves method.
questions.explanation: Since there are \(9\) values, the median is the fifth value, so \(x=9\). The lower half is \(2,3,5,7\), whose median is \(\frac{3+5}{2}=4\). The upper half is \(12,14,16,18\), whose median is \(\frac{14+16}{2}=15\). Therefore, the interquartile range is \(15-4=11\).
questions.hint: Use the median to find \(x\), then find the median of the lower half and the median of the upper half.
